newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ciba welcomes EU approval of gene-maize.
newsitem.headline: Ciba welcomes EU approval of gene-maize.

text.p: Ciba-Geigy AG welcomed the European Commission's approval of gene modified maize for market release, noting that national authorities now have to adapt their local regulations.
"That's good news," a Ciba spokesman said, when asked about the company's reaction to the approval by the EU. He added that Ciba also would issue a written statement later today.

Ciba, which developed the maize to be resistant to corn borers and the herbicide glufosinate, acknowledged some popular resistance to the maize, but the spokesman said the company would seek to address this through open information.
European consumer and environmental groups have urged the EU to reject or at least delay approval on the grounds of uncertainty about the gene-altered maize's possible environmental effects.
Initially Ciba will be marketing the maize to farmers and not consumers, the spokesman said, adding the maize will mainly be used as feed maize.
The maize (corn) has already been approved by U.S. authorities, where it is used on about 0.5 percent of the maize-growing area.
Ciba hopes to double the use of the maize in the next few years in the U.S.
"Initially it won't be a spectacular number in Europe," the spokesman said about the expected usage in Europe.
